title: Lecture 2: Inheritance, Polymorphism and Dynamic Binding
summary: This lecture provides a comprehensive exploration of advanced object-oriented programming mechanisms essential for building flexible and reusable software architectures. Students will master single and multiple inheritance hierarchies, understand polymorphism and substitutability principles, and learn how dynamic binding enables runtime flexibility. Through practical examples in Eiffel and theoretical foundations, students will gain the skills to design extensible class hierarchies and apply these mechanisms to real-world software construction challenges.
learningObjectives: Understand and apply single inheritance to create class hierarchies that promote code reuse and logical organization
Evaluate the benefits and challenges of multiple inheritance and apply appropriate design strategies
Master polymorphism and substitutability principles to write flexible, extensible code
Explain dynamic binding mechanisms and their role in achieving late binding and runtime flexibility
Distinguish between method redefinition and overriding, applying each appropriately
Implement inheritance hierarchies in Eiffel demonstrating best practices in object-oriented design
